sentences.text: We will continue to do our best to mitigate cost pressures for businesses and families.

sections.label: Water pricing components
sections.summary: Pricing in Singapore includes the tariff, waterborne fee and conservation tax.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: That is how it is priced in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: There is the tariff, waterborne fee and the conservation tax.

sections.label: Correction to profit figures
sections.summary: The speaker corrects the average combined SMRT and SBS Transit profit for 2011 to 2022 to $74.6 million a year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
sentences.text: I wish to, first, make a correction to one of the figures I cited in my speech earlier.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
sentences.text: I said between 2011 and 2022, SMRT and SBS Transit together posted profits averaging $55 million a year and reaching $110 million in the last financial year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
sentences.text: For that date range, it should actually be $74.6 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
sentences.text: So, the sentence, should read, "Between 2011 and 2022, SMRT and SBS Transit have together posted profits averaging $74.6 million a year, reaching $110 million in the last financial year." These numbers are from two companies' financial statements.

sections.label: Train operators' financial results
sections.summary: SBST trains make losses of several millions while SMRT trains make a 1% return of $6 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: The trains, I mentioned that the train operators do collect the fares and that is part of their revenue.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: But if we look at the train operations for both SBST and SMRT trains, the numbers, as I shared earlier, SBST making losses of several millions; SMRT trains making a profit of 1% return, $6 million.

sections.label: Vehicle quota target question
sections.summary: The speaker says the difference would not move the needle and asks if the Government will commit to an eventual equal vehicle quota target.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: And by my calculations, it would not move the needle.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: So, if the difference is one of degree, I wonder if the Government will commit to an eventual target of a more or less equal vehicle quota for every year sometime into the future.

sections.label: PHCs treated like taxis
sections.summary: A Member suggests PHCs be treated the same as taxis rather than banned, and asks if the Senior Minister of State agrees.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: Just to be clear, my suggestion was that PHCs should – it is not that they should not be allowed to bid, but they should be treated the same as taxis rather than being banned altogether.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: So, on that, I wonder if Senior Minister of State Chee will agree that the common treatment of PHCs as well as taxi cabs makes much more sense than the current approach.

sections.label: 35% COE injection
sections.summary: A 35% increase is being injected for Cat A and Cat B, in addition to earlier third-quarter injections.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: The injection that we have done, 35% increase for Cat A, 35% increase for Cat B, compared to third quarter, which is injected some already.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: So, this is in addition to that, we are injecting 35%, compared to third quarter.

sections.label: Injection exceeds leasing bids
sections.summary: The 35% injected for Cat A and Cat B is more than the bids won by car-leasing companies in past quarters.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Cat B, I shared also that it is about 23% or thereabouts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: So, what we have injected, 35% for Cat A and Cat B, it is actually more than the bidding, the bids that were won by the car-leasing companies for the past few quarters.

sections.label: Fixed-amount saving incentive
sections.summary: The incentive to save remains because the amount is fixed and not embedded in the price like a price subsidy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: So, the incentive to want to save is still there because it is a fixed amount.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: It is not embedded in the price, unlike a price subsidy, whereby if I consume more, actually, I do end up getting a higher quantum of subsidies because it is embedded in the price.

sections.label: Government rejects profit-seeking claim
sections.summary: The Government rejects the profit-seeking claim, saying it absorbed costs, spent $300 million and gives $2 billion yearly for public transport.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: But I reject what Mr Leong has said, that the Government is profit-seeking.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: We passed through less than one third and we absorbed the rest, because we understand that in this current environment, we do not want to add further stresses on Singaporean families.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: And this cost the Government $300 million to plug the delta, the 15.6%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: And on top of that, every year we give $2 billion for public transport, $1 billion thereabouts for bus, $1 billion for MRT.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: So, Sir, I respectfully ask Mr Leong to withdraw that comment as I think it is not fair and it is not the right way to describe the way the Government operates or to conduct this debate.

sections.label: Bus services not profitable
sections.summary: Almost all bus services running on the roads today are not making profit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Almost all the bus services that are running on our roads today are not making profit.

sections.label: Bus and MRT subsidies
sections.summary: The Government provides $1 billion each for bus and MRT subsidies to sustain the service despite it not making money.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: We continue to run that service even though it is not making money.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: And then to make sure that we are able to run this on a sustained basis, the Government then provides the subsidies to the tune of $1 billion for bus and $1 billion for MRT.

sections.label: Water pricing and U-Save rebates
sections.summary: Water demand is mainly from households; everyone pays full price from the first drop, with means-tested U-Save rebates for households but none for businesses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: The demand for water in Singapore is predominantly actually from households.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Contrary to what Mr Leong seems to have understood, it is actually the other way round.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: We charge everyone the full price of water from the first drop and then we give means-tested subsidies through U-Save rebates to households, lower-income households getting more but for businesses, they do not get any U-Save rebates.

sections.label: Water charging and cost-of-living support
sections.summary: Businesses and households pay the true cost of water from the first drop, businesses get no U-Save rebates, and a $1.1 billion Cost-of-Living Support Package was announced.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: But if the data is the other way round, I apologise for the factual error.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: But it does not change the point I was making and I hope Mr Leong can agree with me on that, that we charge businesses and households the true cost of water from the first drop and we do not provide U-Save rebates to the businesses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: That part I can confirm and double confirm.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Therefore, the issue of cost of living has been a core priority in this House this year, and I, as well as other Members, have previously raised it, together with the impact of high interest rates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: It is evidently front-and-centre in the Government's policy making efforts with the announcement of the $1.1 billion Cost-of-Living Support Package last month, building on the Assurance Package, and other measures announced at Budget 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Singaporeans will be receiving at least $400 in cash and CDC vouchers, with lower income Singaporeans receiving up to $800 cash in December 2023.

sections.label: Strong SGD currency policy
sections.summary: MAS tightened monetary policy five times, including two off-cycle moves, to contain imported cost pressures, a view some economists expect to be sustained.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The effectiveness of a strong SGD currency policy, for instance, as result of MAS tightening monetary policy five times in a row, including in two off-cycle moves last year, has enabled MAS to contain imported cost pressures, and some economists such as OCBC’s chief economist is of the view that this will be sustained for several quarters ahead.

sections.label: Category D COE prices
sections.summary: Category D COE prices dropped from over $13,000 in November 2022 and remain around $11,000 in the recent bidding exercise.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The price of Category D COEs has dropped from over $13,000 in November 2022 and remains at around $11,000 in the recent bidding exercise.

sections.label: Aid for Toa Payoh families
sections.summary: The aim is to help up to about 500 low- to middle-income families, with close to 200 given out so far, benefiting Lorong 7 and Lorong 8 Toa Payoh merchants and hawkers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The aim is to target low- to middle- income residents, as I mentioned.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I think we expect to help up to about 500 families from last September in 2022 when we first launched up to end of this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: So far, we have given out close to about 200 and has benefited merchants and hawkers at Lorong 7 and Lorong 8 Toa Payoh.

sections.label: Transport concessions and vouchers
sections.summary: It highlights a 10% cut in monthly concession pass costs, a new discounted pass for Workfare Transport Concession cardholders, and $50 Public Transport Vouchers for lower-income households.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: That is quite important and he has shared this with the House last month as well.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: But what is key are actually the 10% reduction in the cost of monthly concession passes, implementation of a new discounted monthly pass for Workfare Transport Concession cardholders and the $50 Public Transport Vouchers for lower-income households.

sections.label: U-Save rebates offsetting utility bills
sections.summary: Over two years, additional U-Save rebates will on average fully offset utility bill increases for 1- to 2-room HDB flats, about 80% for 3- to 4-room flats, and about 65% for larger flats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Over the next two years, the additional U-Save rebates will, on average, fully offset the increase in utility bills for 1- to 2-room HDB flats, about 80% for 3- to 4-room HDB flats, and about 65% for larger flats.

sections.label: Egg price increase since 2021
sections.summary: Official data shows egg prices rose by almost 40% in the 20 months since July 2021.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: (In Mandarin):   Official data shows that since July 2021, which is in the past 20 months, the price of eggs has gone up by almost 40%.

sections.label: Price and GST increases
sections.summary: In the last two years, overall prices rose by more than 10%, while GST rose by one percentage point.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: In the last two years, prices have gone up by more than 10% overall, but during this period, GST have gone up by one percentage point.

sections.label: Exchange rate offsetting inflation
sections.summary: Strengthening the Singapore dollar exchange rate offset 2.5% of inflation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: Through strengthening the Singapore dollar exchange rate, we have managed to offset 2.5% of inflation.

sections.label: PWM and low-income wages
sections.summary: Because of PWM, low-income Singaporeans' wages rose by 2.9% annually between 2017 and 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: Because of PWM, between 2017 and 2022, the wages of low-income Singaporeans have increased by 2.9% annually.

sections.label: Hawker food price increases
sections.summary: The passage states other Singaporeans are enjoying wage increases and that hawker food prices rose by 13% on average in the past two years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: After all, other Singaporeans are enjoying wage increases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: I believe that in the past two years, hawker food prices have increased by 13% on average.

sections.label: Workfare and PWM wage support
sections.summary: Workfare provides direct payouts to low-income Singaporeans, and with PWM the Government supplements wage increases while guiding businesses and consumers to share cost increases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: Regardless whether they are low-income workers or self-employed persons, Government has another major initiative - Workfare.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: This provides direct payout to those Singaporeans who earn low income and it helps to supplement their income.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: Through Workfare and PWM, on one hand, the Government directly supplements part of the wage increase of low-income Singaporeans; on the other hand, it guides businesses and consumers to take on part of the increase in cost through market.

sections.label: MAS inflation expectations
sections.summary: MAS expected CPI-All Items inflation to average around 5% in 2023, down from 6.1% the year before, and 3.0% to 4.0% in 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In its October Monetary Policy Statement, the MAS shared its expectations for Consumer Price Index (CPI)-All Items inflation to average around 5% in 2023, down from 6.1% the year before, and for the inflation rate to average between 3.0% to 4.0% in 2024.

sections.label: GST revenue increase
sections.summary: Even with a one-percentage point GST increase, the Government expects GST revenues in FY2023 to be $2.9 billion higher than FY2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Even with a one-percentage point increase in the GST thus far, the Government expects GST revenues in FY2023 to be $2.9 billion higher than FY2022.

sections.label: HDB resale price rise
sections.summary: HDB resale prices rose about 1.3% in the third quarter of 2023, and since 2020 have cumulatively risen 36% versus 28% for private housing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Based on the latest third quarter 2023 data, HDB resale prices continued its ascent, up about 1.3% from the last quarter, with the increase higher than the 1.2% quarter-on-quarter increase initially estimated for the quarter.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This is despite additional cooling measures introduced more than a year ago in September 2022 involving tighter housing loan criteria and a new wait-out period of 15 months for current and former owners of private residential property to buy a non-subsidised HDB resale flat.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In each year since 2020, public housing price increases have outpaced that of the private residential market.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: And cumulatively, we have seen resale HDB prices up by 36%, compared to private residential at 28% since the start of 2020.

sections.label: Private residential rent increases
sections.summary: The passage states private residential rents are up 19% from a year ago and close to 59% over three years, though rental growth has moderated.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I agree with the Member's call and have, in March this year, also called on the Government to support Singaporeans intending to rent a house in the open market and to consider mechanisms to moderate rents in the housing market.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: But while rental growth rates have moderated, compared to a year ago, private residential rents are up by 19%, well above overall inflation rates and up by close to 59% over the last three years.

sections.label: Sengkang 4-room flat rentals
sections.summary: Median rentals for a 4-room HDB flat in Sengkang are now $3,200 a month, compared to less than $2,000 three years ago.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Median rentals for a 4-room HDB flat in Sengkang, for example, is now at $3,200 a month compared to less than $2,000 three years ago.

sections.label: BTO flat supply averages
sections.summary: The average of 20,000 BTO flats from 2021 to 2025 is above the 17,000 from 2016 to 2020 but 13% below the 23,000 from 2011 to 2015.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Moreover, while the average of 20,000 BTO flats between 2021 to 2025 is an increase compared to average of 17,000 flats between 2016 and 2020, this is still 13% below the average of 23,000 flats in 2011 to 2015, during the time when Mr Khaw Boon Wan was the Ministry of National Development (MND) Minister and sought to address the backlog in HDB flats.

sections.label: Keeping up BTO launches
sections.summary: Instead of cutting BTO flat supply by close to 20% from 2024, the current pace of launches should be kept up.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Rather than reduce the supply of BTO flats by close to 20% from 2024 onwards, we ought to ensure that we keep up with the current pace of launches, and this is only just about in line with the average of 23,000 flats from 2011 to 2015.

sections.label: Rental flats under management
sections.summary: As at FY2022 there were 63,681 rental flats under management, a net increase of about 541 in five years, with only 900 public rental flats under construction.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: As at FY2022, there were 63,681 rental flats under management, a net increase of about 541 flats in the five years since FY2018.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The pace of development of rental flats is expected to slow down even further, where there are only 900 public rental flats currently under construction and will be completed in the next five years.

sections.label: Housing demand and population growth
sections.summary: Demand appears higher than previously expected, with Singapore's population growing 5% to 5.92 million as of June 2023, the fastest since 2008.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: While the supply side solutions I have proposed to address the current predicament are not new per se, and various WP MPs, including myself, have called for this during the Housing Motion debate and MND Committee of Supply debates in recent years, what is worth highlighting is that demand appears to be much higher than what was previously expected; or at least what I had previously expected.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: It appears that Singapore's population grew at 5% to 5.92 million as of June 2023, the fastest growth rate since 2008.

sections.label: Housing demand, lease decay, GST
sections.summary: With declining household sizes, elevated housing demand may be more permanent, and the passage raises HDB lease expiry and delaying the GST hike.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Coupled with the steady decline in average household sizes, it now appears that elevated levels of housing demand are likely to be more permanent than transient, and we need to better prepare our housing market for this reality.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Even as we debate the issue of soaring housing prices today, we cannot be silent on the eventuality of the value of HDB flats reaching zero at the end of the 99-year lease, as this will simply mean that the higher the rise in prices today, the harder the fall eventually.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In this cost-of-living crisis, when we have already achieved the revenue growth expected from the GST hike, will delaying the GST hike until 2024, even only for a year, bring more problems for the future as the Government has said?

sections.label: Population growth and housing supply
sections.summary: If population growth continues, public housing supply may decrease by nearly 20% from 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: If the population growth rate continues, we may face even bigger problems as public housing supply will decrease by nearly 20% from 2024.

sections.label: Punggol budget meals and kopi
sections.summary: Punggol Merchants' Association introduced $3 budget meals and a free kopi programme card, and MND introduced budget meals at HDB-owned coffeeshops.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Our Punggol Merchants' Association sprung into action and introduced, with the help of our residents, $3 budget meals at all Punggol Shore food court stalls.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: One food court operator took it further and partnered with the National Taxi Association with the introduction of a free kopi programme card to address the livelihood crunch that our drivers face.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Such budget meals and kopi programmes are popular and welcomed, and I understand that the MND has introduced budget meals at all HDB-owned coffeeshops.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Can we also consider getting privately-owned coffeeshops to also offer budget meals, perhaps through their Merchant Associations?

sections.label: Unity amid global challenges
sections.summary: It urges continued unity as stakeholders in building Singapore's community, economy and lives with kindness and resolve despite global challenges.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: As the dust settles, let us continue to be united stakeholders in building our Singapore community, economy and lives with kindness and resolve, even when we have global challenges looms ahead.

sections.label: HDB delayed flats and new launches
sections.summary: HDB has completed close to 75% of pandemic-delayed projects, should finish the rest by early 2025, and plans up to 100,000 new flats from 2021 to 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: To date, HDB has completed close to 75% of the projects delayed by the pandemic and should complete the rest of the delayed flats by early 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: And we are committed to launch up to 100,000 new flats between 2021 and 2025.

sections.label: BTO supply and cooling measures
sections.summary: Catch-up in BTO supply will help moderate resale demand, and two rounds of cooling measures were implemented in December 2021 and September 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: The catch-up in BTO supply will help moderate demand for resale units as people move into the homes they have booked.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: We have implemented two rounds of cooling measures in December 2021 and September 2022.

sections.label: First-time buyers' mortgage servicing ratio
sections.summary: In 2022, eight in 10 first-time BTO and resale flat buyers had an MSR of 25% or less at key collection.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: In 2022, eight in 10 first time home buyers of BTO and resale flats had a Mortgage Servicing Ratio (MSR) of 25% or less upon key collection.

sections.label: 100,000 flats launch commitment
sections.summary: Launching 100,000 flats from 2021 to 2025 means a commitment of 20,000 flats per year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Launching 100,000 flats from 2021 to 2025 which I mentioned previously means a commitment of 20,000 flats per year.

sections.label: Rental options and rent stabilising
sections.summary: Public rental options remain, PPHS flats rise to 4,000 by 2025, and private and public housing rent increases moderated in Q2 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: But we will, first, make sure that there are still public rental options for those who are unable to attain the goal of home ownership.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Also, we are ramping up supply for the Parenthood Provisional Housing Scheme (PPHS).

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: We will have close to 2,000 PPHS flats at the end of this year and we seek to double this to 4,000 by 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: In terms of how the rents are moving in response to the various measures that have been undertaken, I would like to share that private and public housing rents are showing signs of stabilising.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: In the second quarter of 2023, the increase in private and public housing rents moderated to 2.8% and 3.0% respectively, as compared to 7.2% and 4.4% in the previous quarter and we expect this to further ease as more homes are completed and become ready for their owners to move into.

sections.label: Budget meals at HDB coffeeshops
sections.summary: About 114 HDB rental eating houses offer budget meals and drinks, and by 2026 all 374 HDB rental coffeeshops will offer budget meals.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Currently, some 114 HDB rental eating houses offer budget meals and drinks.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: And by 2026, budget meals will be offered at all 374 HDB rental coffeeshops.

sections.label: Rental discount for budget meals
sections.summary: HDB offers a 5% rental discount off market valuation-based renewal rents for one year, subject to verification that new budget meals and drinks were implemented.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: To ease the transition for them, HDB has also offered a rental discount of 5% off the market valuation-based renewal rents for a period of one year from the time of the tenancy being renewed, subject to verification that the new budget meals and drinks have been implemented.

sections.label: Committee Against Profiteering feedback cases
sections.summary: The Committee Against Profiteering has received over 350 feedback submissions, with 32 cases of GST misrepresentation found and resolved.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: To date, the Committee Against Profiteering (CAP), which I note Ms Hazel Poa also sits in, has received over 350 feedback submissions, of which 32 cases have been found to involve GST misrepresentation and which have been resolved.

sections.label: Mandatory retail leasing code
sections.summary: Parliament passed a Bill mandating tenants and landlords of qualifying retail premises comply with the Code of Conduct for Leasing of Retail Premises, effective early February 2024.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: The Parliament has passed a Bill mandating that tenants and landlords of qualifying retail premises comply with the leasing principles set out in the Code of Conduct for Leasing of Retail Premises in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: The Act will take effect in early February 2024 as sufficient time has to be given for the industry to transition to mandatory compliance.

sections.label: Inflation, cost of living, Assurance Package
sections.summary: The Government enhanced the Assurance Package to help households cope with cost of living pressure as inflation moderates.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Right now, inflation is moderating, but we recognise that many households still feel the pressure from cost of living.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: That is why the Government has enhanced the Assurance Package to help everyone cope better.

sections.label: Assurance Package delays GST impact
sections.summary: The Assurance Package delayed the GST increase's impact by at least five years for most Singaporean households and about 10 years for lower-income households.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: With the Assurance Package, we have delayed the impact of the GST increase for the majority of Singaporean households by at least five years and by about 10 years for lower-income households.

sections.label: Increase in persons over one year
sections.summary: The increase was close to about 280,000 or 290,000 persons in the last one year versus about 28,000 to 29,000 in the last five years' average prior to COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: If you look at it in absolute terms, I think the number is close to about 280,000 or 290,000 persons' increase in the last one year versus the increase of about 28,000 to 29,000 in the last five years' average. prior to COVID-19.

sections.label: HDB clearing COVID-19 delayed projects backlog
sections.summary: In response to Mr Louis Chua's questions, HDB has delivered close to 75% of the COVID-19 delayed projects while clearing the backlog.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: In response to Mr Louis Chua's questions, first of all, in terms of backlog, I have shared that we are in the process of clearing the backlog and that HDB has delivered close to 75% of the COVID-19 delayed projects.

sections.label: HDB deficit and taxpayer-funded subsidies
sections.summary: HDB reported a $5.38 billion deficit, largely due to subsidies to BTO buyers, and these deficits are taxpayer-funded.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: One, the HDB recently reported a $5.38 billion dollars deficit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: A lot of this is probably due to the subsidies given to the BTO buyers because HDB paid $5.9 billion to the Singapore Land Authority (SLA) at the same time in the same year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Actually, I am very glad that Mr Leong seems to have come round to the idea that there is a deficit in our building programme and the deficit is made up by the subsidies that are given to Singaporeans; so, the answer is yes, these deficits are taxpayer-funded.

sections.label: Review and Affordable Housing Scheme comparison
sections.summary: Evolving circumstances prompt a review, but the comparison asked is spurious because the Affordable Housing Scheme seeks to reconcile three incompatible aims.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: As with every Government scheme, when circumstances evolve and change, it does prompt a review.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: However, I think that the comparison that Mr Leong is asking me to make is a spurious one because the Affordable Housing Scheme, as I have said before, is one which I do not think has convinced Members of this House or even many members of the public because it seeks to reconcile three quite incompatible aims.

sections.label: Scheme and Reserves debate
sections.summary: The scheme seeks to avoid being seen as a raid on the Reserves, but taking land cost out at first purchase already impacts the Reserves.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: And then also, the scheme seeks to avoid being seen as a raid on the Reserves.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: But as I have said these three aims are not compatible because by taking land cost out at the point of first purchase actually that already has an impact on the Reserves.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: This topic has been covered quite extensively over more than a day of debate in this House, so I do not propose to go through it again.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: But I do not see how I can make any meaningful comparison from between a scheme that has worked, and which requires adjustments from time to time to meet changing circumstances and evolving demand, with a scheme which, as far as we can tell, is actually not able to be internally consistent and is not one that has been convincing to both Members of this House and the public.

sections.label: Housing prices and subsidies
sections.summary: Mr Leong is accused of tying himself in knots over housing price increases and the HDB deficit, implying he denies housing should be subsidised.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Senior Minister of State Sim, would you like to respond to that last clarification by Mr Leong?

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: I think Mr Leong is tying himself up in knots because if he considers the increase in housing prices over the years as a disadvantage of the scheme, is Mr Leong saying that prices must remain static in order for the housing market to be considered favourable and in order for our housing policy to be considered a success?

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: In which case, I think Mr Leong did not pay attention when I explained that with favourable economic conditions and growing wages over time, we do expect to see a gradual increase in home values and prices.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: The second way in which he is tying himself up in knots is that by posing this question about deficit, the deficit incurred by HDB, to me, it seems to me that Mr Leong is denying that housing should be subsidised at all.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: In the case of housing, it is not 100% subsidised by Government; there is some payment from home owners.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: But the subsidy from Government and by extension taxpayers is very substantial; and therefore, it seems to me that Mr Leong's line of questioning will inevitably lead him to conclude that there should not be any subsidy.

sections.label: WP rejects Liang's amendment
sections.summary: The Workers' Party rejects Mr Liang Eng Hua Hwa's amendment, saying its proposals would not undermine fiscal sustainability or burden future generations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: The Workers' Party (WP) rejects the amendment proposed by Member Mr Liang Eng Hua Hwa.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: A careful examination of our proposals today would show that they would neither undermine Singapore's fiscal sustainability nor would they unduly burden future generations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: However, we disagree with Amendment Nos 1 and 2.

sections.label: WP urges policy review
sections.summary: The WP Members of Parliament urge the Government to conduct a comprehensive review of policies to better support Singaporeans during the cost of living crisis.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: The WP Members of Parliament have made concrete proposals in several areas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: We urge the Government to conduct a comprehensive review of its policies to better support Singaporeans and their families during this cost of living crisis.

sections.label: Louis Chua on GST deferment
sections.summary: Mr Louis Chua reiterated his call for the Government to defer the 2024 GST hike, noting the revenue increase was already achieved.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: Sengkang GRC Member of Parliament, Mr Louis Chua reiterated his call for the Government to defer the GST hike in 2024, with even one year being a helpful deferment, especially when the Government has already achieved the revenue increase which the GST hike was meant to bring.

sections.label: Jamus Lim on COE system
sections.summary: Assoc Prof Jamus Lim called for changes to the COE system to rationalise high prices, affecting households and taxi or PHC users.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: On private transport, Sengkang GRC Member of Parliament, Assoc Prof Jamus Lim called for changes to the COE system that would rationalise high prices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: He explained why expensive COE affect not just households that may have very legitimate need for cars, such as families with children or the disabled, but also everyone that books a taxi or PHC.

sections.label: Public transport corporation proposal
sections.summary: Gerald Giam called for a publicly owned non-profit National Transport Corporation to plan and operate all MRT, LRT and trunk bus services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: On public transport, Aljunied GRC Member, Mr Gerald Giam called for a National Transport Corporation to be established as a publicly owned non-profit land transport planner and operator of all MRT, LRT and trunk bus services.

sections.label: Lowering HDB prices
sections.summary: The Government will look to lower HDB prices through the deployment of taxpayer dollars.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: The reality, Mr Speaker, is that the Government will look to lower HDB prices through the deployment of taxpayer dollars.

sections.label: Workers' Party voting position
sections.summary: The Workers' Party will vote in favour of the original Motion and reject the amended Motion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: The Workers' Party will vote in favour of the original Motion and reject the amended Motion for the reasons I have provided earlier in my round-up speech.

sections.label: Amendment No 1 text
sections.summary: Amendment No 1 inserts words acknowledging that cost of living is a global concern.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Amendment No 1 is, "In line 1, after the words 'That this House' to insert the words 'acknowledges that cost of living is a global concern, and'".

sections.label: Amendment No 2 text
sections.summary: Amendment No 2 deletes 'review its policies so as to' and inserts 'continue pursuing policies that together'.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Amendment No 2 is, "In line 1, to delete 'review its policies so as to' and insert 'continue pursuing policies that together'".

sections.label: Amendment No 3 and question
sections.summary: Amendment No 3 adds words on fiscal sustainability and future generations, and the question is stated.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Amendment No 3 is, "At the end of line 2, to add ', without undermining our fiscal sustainability and burdening future generations of Singaporeans'''.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: The question is, "That this House acknowledges that cost of living is a global concern, and calls on the Government to continue pursuing policies that together lower cost of living pressures on Singaporeans and their families, without undermining our fiscal sustainability and burdening future generations of Singaporeans".
